title: Poll: Le Pen begins presidential campaign in strongest position ever amid worried, angry electorate
subhead: In France's polarized political landscape, Marine Le Pen of the far-right Rassemblement National is enjoying unprecedented support, and radical left candidate Jean-Luc Mélenchon is building a strong base. Wide open for other candidates, the race is drawing significant interest from voters concerned about the future, Le Monde's first poll shows.

subhead: Candidates and the climate (3/5). Touting himself as the 'environmental transformation' candidate, Raphaël Glucksmann plans to use decarbonization to reindustrialize France and create jobs by expanding the renewable energy sector.

title: Le Pen pledges to put French citizens first at presidential campaign launch
subhead: Currently ahead in opinion polls, French far-right leader Marine Le Pen told supporters at a political rally on Sunday she would ensure citizens had 'more rights' than foreigners if she were to win next year's presidential election.

title: Venice Film Festival: May el-Toukhy's 'Woman Unknown' wins Golden Lion at politically charged edition
subhead: The Danish-Egyptian director paid tribute to 'invisible and voiceless women.' Ilia Khrjanovski dedicated his Silver Lion 'to Ukrainians fighting for freedom,' while Israeli filmmakers Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor received the Special Jury Prize for their documentary about civilians killed by the Israeli army in Gaza.

title: Trump seeks to play peacemaker in a divided Libya
subhead: After 15 years of keeping a low profile on Libya, Washington now wants to reconcile the rival authorities in the country's east and west by brokering a power-sharing agreement negotiated among a handful of local warlords. Far from calming the nation, this initiative has triggered a frantic reshuffling of power dynamics and exposed the fragility of alliances on both sides.

How 9/11 changed the far right
subhead: The September 11 terrorist attacks marked a turning point for radical right-wing movements. Since then, these political currents have adopted a violently anti-Islam rhetoric, positioning themselves as defenders of a so-called 'Judeo-Christian West.'

title: French government pushes for mandatory helmets for electric scooters, struggles with bicycles
subhead: State authorities around the country are increasingly requiring electric scooter users to wear helmets. Cycling advocacy groups argue such a rule would be counterproductive and would not protect cyclists in most potentially fatal accidents.

title: Hedge funds increasingly speculate on French debt, raising specter of crisis
subhead: Hedge funds now account for more than half of all European bond trading. France, which carries one of the highest debt levels in Western Europe, has become concerned about these creditors, whose profiles are less predictable than those of public institutions, banks or insurers.
